title: Scalable E-commerce Platform
architectureText:
This e-commerce platform follows a microservices architecture deployed on AWS, designed to handle 1M monthly active users with the ability to scale to 10M during peak events.

**Core Design Principles:**
1. **Service Independence**: Each microservice owns its data and can be deployed independently
2. **Event-Driven Communication**: Services communicate asynchronously via Kafka for loose coupling
3. **CQRS Pattern**: Separate read and write models for high-traffic catalog queries
4. **Multi-Region**: Active-passive setup with Route53 failover for disaster recovery

**Data Flow:**
- User requests hit CloudFront CDN for static assets
- API Gateway routes to appropriate microservices via ALB
- Services use PostgreSQL RDS for transactional data
- ElastiCache (Redis) for session management and caching
- OpenSearch for product search functionality
- S3 for product images and static content

**Scaling Strategy:**
- EKS with HPA for automatic pod scaling
- RDS read replicas for database read scaling
- ElastiCache cluster mode for cache scaling
- Kafka partitioning for event stream scaling

services.name: API Gateway
services.description: Entry point for all client requests. Handles authentication, rate limiting, and request routing.

services.name: User Service
services.description: User authentication, profile management, and session handling. Integrates with Cognito for OAuth.

services.name: Product Catalog Service
services.description: Product information management with CQRS. Write model uses PostgreSQL, read model uses OpenSearch.

services.name: Inventory Service
services.description: Real-time inventory tracking with event sourcing. Handles stock reservations and updates.

services.name: Cart Service
services.description: Shopping cart management with Redis for fast access. Handles cart expiration and recovery.

services.name: Order Service
services.description: Order processing orchestrator using Saga pattern. Coordinates payment, inventory, and shipping.

services.name: Payment Service
services.description: Payment processing with Stripe and PayPal integration. Handles refunds and disputes.

services.name: Search Service
services.description: Product search and filtering using OpenSearch. Supports faceted search and autocomplete.

services.name: Recommendation Service
services.description: ML-based product recommendations using SageMaker. Collaborative filtering and content-based.

services.name: Notification Service
services.description: Email, SMS, and push notifications. Handles order updates and marketing campaigns.

scalingStrategy.description: Multi-tier auto-scaling with EKS HPA for services, RDS read replicas for database, and ElastiCache cluster mode for caching. Kafka partitions scale with consumer groups.

securityRecommendations.recommendation: Deploy services in private subnets with NAT Gateway for outbound traffic. Use VPC endpoints for AWS services.
Use Cognito with MFA for user authentication. Implement JWT with short expiry (15min) and refresh tokens.
Enable encryption at rest for RDS, ElastiCache, and S3. Use KMS managed keys.
Implement rate limiting at API Gateway level. Use WAF rules to block common attack patterns.
PCI-DSS compliance: Never store card data. Use Stripe/PayPal tokenization. Audit all payment transactions.
Enable CloudTrail for API audit logging. Set up alerts for suspicious activities and failed authentications.

costEstimate.breakdown:
Compute (EKS): 35% (~$3,500)
Database (RDS): 25% (~$2,500)
Cache (ElastiCache): 10% (~$1,000)
Messaging (MSK): 10% (~$1,000)
Search (OpenSearch): 8% (~$800)
Network & CDN: 7% (~$700)
Storage & Other: 5% (~$500)
costEstimate.assumptions: Based on 1M MAU, 50GB database, 20GB cache, moderate Kafka throughput. Costs will increase 2-3x during peak events. Reserved instances can reduce costs by 30-40%.
